issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a SealSaloon constructor that takes a String parameter (SealSaloon(String)), but both the provided template usage (Main.java) and the reference solution implement and use a no-argument constructor (SealSaloon()). This constructor-parameter mismatch will confuse students about which constructor signature to implement and which the tests expect.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor requirement consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement and UML to require a no-argument constructor (SealSaloon()) to match the template and solution, or (B) change the template Main and the solution SealSaloon to use/implement SealSaloon(String name). Ensure the problem text, UML, template examples, and tests all use the same constructor signature.

issues.description: The problem text instructs students to initialize the stock attribute in the SealSaloon constructor (per-instance), but elsewhere (and in the reference solution) the stock attribute is required to be static (shared across all instances) and is initialized at declaration. This is an internal contradiction in the specification about the lifecycle and initialization of the stock attribute.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify and align the specification: either require stock to be an instance (non-static) field and specify initialization in the constructor, or require stock to be static/shared and specify that it should be initialized at declaration or in a static initializer. Update the problem text and UML so they consistently state whether stock is static and how it should be initialized.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies a SealSaloon constructor signature that takes a String parameter (+SealSaloon(String)) for the saloon name, but both the provided template usage and the reference solution implement/use a no-argument constructor (new SealSaloon()). This API mismatch (constructor signature) creates confusion about the required constructor and whether a name field must be stored, making it unclear to students which constructor to implement and how to map the description to the code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor requirement consistent: either update the problem statement to require a no-argument constructor (SealSaloon()) or update the template and solution to provide a constructor SealSaloon(String name) that stores the name (and add a corresponding getter). Prefer adding a String-parameter constructor in the code (and keeping a no-arg overload if desired) so the implementation matches the problem description and examples.
